channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Photobiomodulation therapy has a negligible effect as an adjunct to motor control exercise in people with chronic non-specific low back pain: a randomised trial.
item.description: Adding photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) to motor control exercise (MCE) provided negligible additional improvements in pain intensity (MD -0.4 points), disability (MD -0.7 points), or circulating PGE2 concentrations compared with sham PBMT plus MCE at 6 weeks and throughout 12-month follow-up in 148 adults with chronic non-specific low back pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Association Between Early Postoperative Limb Symmetry Index Scores and 2-Year Patient-Reported Outcomes After Quadriceps Tendon Autograft ACL Reconstruction.
item.description: In 100 patients after quadriceps tendon autograft ACL reconstruction, 3-month isometric quadriceps LSI strongly predicted 2-year IKDC scores (β = 3.9, Adj R² = 0.36), while 9-month fast quadriceps LSI strongly predicted both Lysholm and IKDC scores (β = 3.9-4.7, Adj R² = 0.34-0.35).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Post burn Cubital Tunnel Syndrome Electrophysiological and Functional Responses to High intensity Laser Therapy versus Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: In 75 patients with post-burn cubital tunnel syndrome, both HILT+UNGE and ESWT+UNGE improved nerve conduction and upper-limb function more than UNGE alone. HILT resulted in significantly greater improvements than ESWT across all electrophysiological outcomes and DASH scores, with benefits maintained at 12-week follow-up.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The effect of functional inspiratory muscle training on diaphragm function and core stabilisation in patients with chronic non-specific low back pain: a randomised controlled trial
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (N=40) found that a 10-week multicomponent functional inspiratory muscle training (F-IMT) program significantly improved diaphragm thickness (adjusted difference, 2.434 mm; 95% CI, 1.714 to 3.261; P < .001) and mobility, reduced pain, and increased respiratory muscle strength and core endurance in patients with chronic non-specific low back pain, compared to thoracic expansion exercises.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Credibility and strength of evidence for exercise, nutritional, and combined interventions on muscle function and physical performance in older adults: an umbrella review of meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials
item.description: An umbrella review of meta-analyses found the strongest evidence for exercise interventions in older adults, especially for fall prevention. Nutrition-only interventions may modestly benefit muscle mass in specific populations, and combined interventions show some promise for strength and function.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Effects of extracorporeal shockwave therapy on pain intensity and functional disability in chronic low back pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 9 RCTs (N=430) found that radial extracorporeal shockwave therapy (rESWT) significantly reduced pain in chronic low back pain (SMD = -0.72; 95% CI -1.30 to -0.14), but functional improvements (MD = -6.12) did not meet the minimal clinically important difference.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical activity guidelines' impact on cognition in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 RCTs (N=462) found that meeting physical activity guidelines for people with multiple sclerosis (MS) significantly improved processing speed (SMD = 0.29), visuospatial memory (SMD = 0.47), and verbal memory (SMD = 0.75).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of treadmill exercise with and without vertical traction on gait, pain, disability, trunk proprioception, and depression in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain: A randomized controlled trial.
item.description: Adding vertical traction and partial body weight support to treadmill exercise improved gait, disability, and trunk repositioning more than treadmill exercise alone in chronic low back pain patients (n=45).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes and Factors Associated With Response in Older Adults With Massive Irreparable Rotator Cuff Tears: A Four-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
item.description: In older adults (≥60 yrs) with atraumatic massive irreparable rotator cuff tears (MIRCTs), 95-97% achieved minimal clinically important difference after 12 weeks of nonoperative treatment, sustained to 4 years; longer symptom duration and smoking were associated with worse function.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of Sensory Electrical Stimulation Versus Alternating Electromyography-Guided Electrical Stimulation on Functional Recovery of the Hand in Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: In chronic stroke patients (n=60), sensory electrical stimulation (SES) and alternating EMG-guided electrical stimulation (Alt-EMG) combined with conventional therapy improved upper-limb function, spasticity, and strength significantly more than conventional therapy alone, with no difference between SES and Alt-EMG.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Can Psychological Readiness Predict Successful Return to Sports After Patellar Stabilization Surgery in Adolescent Patients? A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: In adolescent patients undergoing patellar stabilization surgery, an ACL-RSI score ≥59.2 is a significant predictor of successful return to sports, independent of injury characteristics.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Clinical and functional outcomes of aquatic plyometrics in adolescent patellofemoral pain syndrome: a dual-arm randomized controlled trial | Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine
item.description: A dual-arm RCT found aquatic plyometric exercises significantly improved pain, quadriceps and hamstring torque, functional disability, and quality of life in adolescents with patellofemoral pain syndrome compared to conventional exercises.
item.author: J Rehabil Med

item.title: Six-month supervised telerehabilitation combining pilates-based therapeutic exercise and self-myofascial release in adults with fibromyalgia: a randomized controlled trial | Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine
item.description: A 6-month supervised telerehabilitation program combining Pilates-based exercise and self-myofascial release significantly improved fibromyalgia impact, sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and perceived stress compared to usual care in adults with fibromyalgia.
item.author: J Rehabil Med

item.title: Effects of Exercise Training on the Metabolic Cost of Walking in Health and Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 27 studies (1177 participants) found that chronic physical exercise training significantly improved the metabolic cost of walking (g = 0.40, p = 0.001) in healthy adults, with smaller non-significant effects in stroke patients, supporting its role in improving walking economy.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: From information to action; co-designing pain neuroscience education for adolescents with low back pain: Focus group insights.
item.description: Co-designing pain neuroscience education for adolescents with low back pain revealed needs for relatable, practical, engaging, and easily navigable content, leading to the Back To Move prototype.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Hybrid versus in-clinic rehabilitation for non-traumatic shoulder pain within a standardized digital care pathway: a prospective longitudinal observational study
item.description: A prospective longitudinal observational study of 164 rehabilitation episodes for non-traumatic shoulder pain found no clear between-modality difference in time to documented clinical discharge or secondary outcomes between hybrid (1 in-clinic, 2 home sessions/week) and in-clinic (3 in-clinic sessions/week) rehabilitation.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Elastic band resistance training improves physical function, gait, cardiac indices, and corticomuscular coherence in older women at risk of sarcopenia: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: In 40 older women at risk of sarcopenia, 12 weeks of elastic band resistance training significantly improved muscle strength, physical function, gait parameters (increased stride length, reduced double-support time), and corticomuscular coherence, alongside positive changes in cardiac morphology and function.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Effect of bimodal signal biofeedback on the supraglottic swallowing maneuver in patients with post-stroke dysphagia: A randomised controlled trial
item.description: A randomized controlled trial investigated the effect of bimodal signal biofeedback, combining an accelerometer and a nasal airflow sensor, on the supraglottic swallowing maneuver in patients with post-stroke dysphagia.
item.author: Archives of PM&R

item.title: Effectiveness of Kalevala Manual Therapy, Health Coaching, and Physiotherapy for Chronic Low Back Pain: A Randomized Controlled Trial (The INTEGRA Trial)
item.description: In a three-arm RCT with 81 adults with non-specific chronic low back pain, Kalevala Manual Therapy (KMT) and KMT combined with health coaching (KMT+HC) showed comparable improvements in pain and functional disability to guideline-based physiotherapy, with KMT+HC also significantly reducing work-related fear-avoidance beliefs.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Trajectories of physical activity following digital education and exercise therapy-a longitudinal registry study among 15,197 persons with knee or hip osteoarthritis.
item.description: A longitudinal registry study of 15,197 individuals with knee or hip osteoarthritis found that participation in a digital education and exercise therapy program increased the proportion reaching recommended physical activity levels from 51.4% to 58.5% at one year. Four distinct physical activity trajectories were identified, with BMI and physical function being key associated factors.
item.author: PubMed
